messages:
emma (docs): FYI I9m seeing a handful of broken fragment links that point to table headers after the migration. linkcheck flagged /guides/cli -> /guides/cli#available-commands-table as 404.

raj (eng): can you paste the exact linkcheck line?

ci-bot: linkcheck: ERROR: broken link at /guides/cli (target /guides/cli#available-commands-table)	60.2% coverage

emma (docs): example from source: in docs/guides/cli.md we have a table under heading: `## Available commands (table)` and other pages link to `#available-commands-table`. on the built site the heading id is `available-commands` (no "-table") so anchors don't match.

mia (devex): that sounds like slugify differences. some slugifiers strip parenthetical words and punctuation. did MkDocs generate the full id before?

emma (docs): yes, mkdocs->python-slugify produced `available-commands-table` previously. docusaurus/remark-slug seems to drop the parentheses table part.

raj (eng): two paths: 1) normalize slugify behavior to the old output (configure remark-slug or use a custom slugify fn) 2) require explicit anchor ids on headings that are targets of cross-page links.

lila (i18n): prefer option 2 for translated pages; translators can add `{#id}` and we avoid changing automated slugs that might differ by locale.

mia (devex): pragmatic plan: run detection to find links that point at missing ids, generate a small redirects map for those specific anchors, add a lint rule that warns when a heading used as a link target doesn't have an explicit `{#id}`.

emma (docs): I can run a grep pass to find `#...-table` usages and match against built HTML ids. a tiny script: ```bash
# list markdown anchors referenced elsewhere
grep -R "#available-commands-table" -n docs/ || true
# verify existence in built html
grep -R "id=\"available-commands-table\"" site/ || echo "missing"
```

raj (eng): I'll add a post-build check that scans `site/` for missing ids and emits `build/anchor-redirects.json` mapping old->actual. we can apply CDN redirects for those few.

mia (devex): and I'll add a markdownlint custom rule: flag any ATX heading that contains the word "table" and is referenced by another file if it lacks `{#...}`. we can autofix most by inserting `{#slug}`.

lila (i18n): I'll run the detector across `i18n/*/docs` to surface translations that may need manual id fixes. we should avoid auto-inserting ids in locale content without a reviewer.

ci-bot: preview build: linkcheck found 3 broken anchors. details in workflow run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/actions/runs/987654321.

emma (docs): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1412 (draft) contains: - detector script - anchor-redirects generator - markdownlint rule + autofixer (opt-in) - contributing update advising `{#explicit-id}` for table headings

preview-bot: staging preview for PR-1412: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-1412	6% decreased broken links (3 -> 0)

raj (eng): will tidy the redirects generator and add a small unit test. planning to emit redirects only for entries flagged by the detector to keep the redirect list tiny.

emma (docs): thanks all 55 can we aim to land this week? tagging @mia for the lint, @raj for redirects, @lila for i18n sign-off.

mia (devex): yes, I9ll open a follow-up PR for the lint rule if this draft looks good.

lila (i18n): will review the i18n report and add comments to the PR with pages needing manual attention.

emma (docs): awesome. once merged I9ll run a full linkcheck sweep and flip the docs-only workflow to fail-on-broken. :shipit:
